clue.text: Reprimand for appearing in casual attire

blocks.note: first meaning: a severe scolding
second meaning: wearing clothes less formal than usual, as on a relaxed office day

explanation.surface: Someone is told off for turning up to work in jeans.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is both a noun for a stern telling-off and the act of wearing informal clothes.

clue.text: Being upset, poured scorn on surrender

indicators.note: in a down entry something upset is turned upside down, so the word reads from bottom to top

blocks.note: abused, insulted

explanation.surface: Someone upset at being mocked over giving in.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry, upset means turned upside down, so the word is read bottom to top.
explanation.definitionFit: To deliver up is to hand over or give up something, as a town is delivered to an enemy.

clue.text: Famous American leading entertainer, lifting voice in song

definitions.text: leading entertainer, lifting voice in song

blocks.note: first meaning: a celebrated person from the United States, known by first name alone

blocks.clueFragment: leading entertainer, lifting voice in song
blocks.note: second meaning: a top performer singing, the man nicknamed the King of rock and roll

explanation.surface: A celebrated American star raises his voice in song.
explanation.definitionFit: Elvis Presley, the American rock and roll star, was a singer famous worldwide by his first name.

clue.text: It's dark, so Scots retire inside

indicators.note: 'inside' places one word within another, as the Scots go indoors

blocks.note: sae is the Scots form of so
to turn in is to go to bed

explanation.surface: Night has fallen, so the Scottish folk head indoors to bed.
explanation.walkthrough: SA(TURN IN)E: the Scots word for so goes round the phrase for going to bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Saturnine describes a gloomy, sombre temperament or look, a figurative sense of dark.

clue.text: Pleasant new girl's best friend

blocks.note: N is short for new
diamonds are a girl's best friend, and ice is slang for diamonds

explanation.surface: A newly arrived girl's best friend is a lovely person.
explanation.definitionFit: Nice and pleasant are everyday synonyms for something agreeable.

clue.text: Find divorces moving

indicators.note: letters that are moving shift position, so the word is rearranged

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Someone finds divorce cases emotionally touching.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moving' reads as touching, but it says the letters move about.
explanation.definitionFit: To find something and to discover it both mean coming upon it for the first time.

clue.text: Welts, i.e. beats soundly

indicators.note: 'soundly' read as 'by sound' means the word is heard, not spelt

blocks.note: to whale is to thrash or flog someone

explanation.surface: Raised marks on the skin, that is, a thorough thrashing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soundly' looks like 'thoroughly', but it means as heard.
explanation.definitionFit: A wale is a ridge raised on flesh by a blow, a variant spelling of weal or welt.

clue.text: Oliver, not fit to be a roue, remains in Avebury

indicators.note: 'not fit' means without a word meaning healthy, so that word is removed

blocks.note: Oliver Cromwell, Lord Protector
in good health
a lecher, a rake

explanation.surface: Oliver, deemed unfit to be a rake, lies buried in Wiltshire.
explanation.walkthrough: Avebury is a Wiltshire village inside a great prehistoric stone circle.
explanation.definitionFit: A cromlech is a prehistoric stone monument, a circle or dolmen, the sort of ancient relic found at Avebury.

clue.text: Fish taking mouse

blocks.note: first meaning: a small silvery freshwater fish
second meaning: slang for a bruised black eye

explanation.surface: A fish catches a mouse.
explanation.definitionFit: A shiner is both a minnow-like fish and a bruised swollen eye, which is also slangily called a mouse.

clue.text: Numbers can be found at the end of this book

definitions.text: Numbers can be found at the end of this book

blocks.clueFragment: Numbers can be found at the end of this book
blocks.note: surface reading: a book with figures or a numbered index at its back
setter's reading: Numbers is a book of the Bible, and it comes straight after the book wanted, the third book of Moses

explanation.surface: A reader notes that the page numbers or tables sit at the back of a book.
explanation.walkthrough: Numbers, capitalised only because it opens the clue, is the fourth book of the Old Testament.
explanation.definitionFit: The third book of the Pentateuch is immediately followed in the Bible by the book of Numbers.

clue.text: Some poplar, chestnut, or other wood

indicators.note: 'some' asks for only part of the words that follow, so a run of letters is taken from them

blocks.note: the end of poplar runs into the start of chestnut

explanation.surface: A list of tree timbers: poplar, chestnut or something else.
explanation.definitionFit: Larch is a conifer whose timber is a familiar wood, a different tree from the two named.

clue.text: Way into actual room used by minister

indicators.note: 'into' puts the way inside the word for actual

blocks.note: St is short for street
very in the old sense of true or real, as in 'the very man'

explanation.surface: Directions to the real room a clergyman uses.
explanation.walkthrough: VE(ST)RY: the street abbreviation sits inside the word for actual.
explanation.definitionFit: A vestry is the church room where the clergy robe and keep vestments and records.

clue.text: Doctor injecting poet with drug

indicators.note: injecting pushes one thing inside another, so the drug goes within the poet

blocks.note: A. E. Housman, author of A Shropshire Lad
E is ecstasy

explanation.surface: A doctor gives a poet an injection of some drug.
explanation.walkthrough: E is a common abbreviation for the drug ecstasy. In Britain a houseman is a junior hospital doctor, roughly an American intern.
explanation.definitionFit: A houseman is a newly qualified physician working in a hospital, so a kind of medic.

clue.text: Given refund when protective clothing's returned

indicators.note: something returned goes back the way it came, so the word reads right to left

blocks.note: a diaper (nappy) protects a baby's clothes

explanation.surface: A shopper gets money back after taking protective overalls back to the shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Returned' looks like a shopper taking goods back; it tells you to read the word backwards. The 's is read as 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who has been given a refund has had their money paid back to them.

clue.text: Stop meeting with professional criminal

blocks.note: short for professional
a villain

explanation.surface: Someone breaks off contact with a career criminal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stop meeting' looks like ending an acquaintance; it is the verb for suspending a parliament's sittings.
explanation.definitionFit: To prorogue a parliament is to discontinue its session without dissolving it.

clue.text: Ducks, for instance, making people use bad language

blocks.note: men as people in general
to curse

explanation.surface: Something about ducks causes people to curse.
explanation.walkthrough: Ducks here are trousers made of duck, a heavy cotton or linen cloth, not birds.
explanation.definitionFit: Duck trousers are garments for males, an example of the clothing category sold to them.

clue.text: Fruit in jelly, in Bristol fashion?

indicators.note: fruit set in a jelly sits within it, so one word goes inside the other

blocks.note: a shape is an old word for a moulded jelly or blancmange
rose hips

explanation.surface: Fruit set in a jelly, served in the style of Bristol.
explanation.walkthrough: A shape is an old British word for a jelly or blancmange set in a mould, which the surface hides by making jelly sound like the dessert itself.
explanation.definitionFit: The sailing phrase 'shipshape and Bristol fashion' pairs the two as meaning neat and in good order.

clue.text: Woman making dire cove free?

indicators.note: letters set free are released from their order, and the word also hints at a wife freed from marriage

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A woman who frees herself from an awful man.
explanation.walkthrough: A cove is an old British slang word for a chap; 'free' both releases the letters and hints at a woman freed from a bad husband.
explanation.definitionFit: A divorcee is a person, here a female one, whose marriage has been legally ended.

clue.text: As coteries might be?

indicators.note: 'might be' asks what else these letters could become when rearranged

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A question about what exclusive little cliques tend to be like.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and the definition: the letters of coteries rearrange, and coteries are themselves inward-looking.
explanation.definitionFit: Esoteric means understood only by a small inner circle, which is what a coterie is.

clue.text: Monarchy political leader turned into republic

indicators.note: a leader turned faces the other way, so the abbreviation is flipped
'into' places the flipped leader inside the republic

blocks.note: Eire is the Irish name for the Republic of Ireland
Prime Minister

explanation.surface: A monarchist's leader becomes a republican.
explanation.walkthrough: E(MP)IRE: the Prime Minister abbreviation is flipped and placed inside the Irish republic.
explanation.definitionFit: An empire is a realm ruled by an emperor or sovereign, so a form of monarchy.

clue.text: Piece of the cloth

blocks.note: first meaning: a chessman that moves diagonally
second meaning: 'the cloth' is the clergy, so a senior churchman

explanation.surface: A scrap cut from a length of fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Piece of the cloth' reads as a remnant of fabric, but it splits into a chess piece and a member of the clergy.
explanation.definitionFit: The chess piece and the senior clergyman who oversees a diocese share the same name.

clue.text: Put on to hand

blocks.note: first meaning: to stage a show or performance
second meaning: nearby and available, here

explanation.definitionFit: To present a play is to stage it, and something present is close by and available.

clue.text: Contemptuously dismiss bears

blocks.note: two of the honey-loving bear from A. A. Milne's stories

explanation.surface: Someone scornfully waves away an idea, which they bear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bears' looks like a verb meaning tolerates; it is a plural noun, two Winnie-the-Poohs.
explanation.definitionFit: To pooh-pooh a suggestion is to scoff at it and treat it as unworthy of notice.

clue.text: Serviceman, in more ways than one

definitions.text: Serviceman, in more ways than one

blocks.note: surface reading: a soldier, sailor or airman
setter's reading: a man in the armed services who also conducts church services, a military chaplain

explanation.walkthrough: Services means both the armed forces and acts of worship, and this man belongs to the first while leading the second.
explanation.definitionFit: Padre is the informal title for a chaplain in the army, navy or air force.

clue.text: Car in extremely fine condition

indicators.note: 'extremely' points to the very end of the word, keeping only its final letter

blocks.note: the final letter of fine
state of repair

explanation.surface: A second-hand car advertised as being in superb condition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extremely fine' reads as very good, but extremely here takes the extreme letter of fine. An estate car is the British name for a station wagon.
explanation.definitionFit: An estate is a type of motor vehicle with a long rear loading area, what Americans call a station wagon.

clue.text: Intimidating a player on the side

blocks.note: taken as written
a winger plays on the flank of a team

explanation.surface: Bullying one of the team's wide players.
explanation.definitionFit: Awing means filling with awe or dread, which overawes and intimidates.

clue.text: Give off while upset

indicators.note: in a down entry upset means overturned, so the word reads from bottom to top

blocks.note: a while is a period of time

explanation.surface: Someone gives off fumes while angry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'While' looks like a conjunction; it is the noun, a spell of time.
explanation.definitionFit: To emit is to send out or discharge, as light, heat or gas.

clue.text: Shot entire sequence

blocks.note: first meaning: a single bullet or shell of ammunition
second meaning: a complete series

explanation.surface: A camera shot that captures a whole run of events.
explanation.definitionFit: A gun fires a round of ammunition, and a round is also one full cycle of events or games.

clue.text: It might produce manic peal

indicators.note: 'might produce' asks what these letters could be made into by rearranging them

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Something that sends out a wild, frantic ringing of bells.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: the letters of manic peal rearrange, and a bell tower is just the thing to send out a frenzied peal.
explanation.definitionFit: A campanile is a bell tower, often freestanding as in Italy, from which bells are rung.

clue.text: Record a great deal about incident with the old

indicators.note: 'about' means around, so the phrase for a lot goes round the others

blocks.note: as in 'a sight better', meaning a lot
something that happens
ye is an archaic spelling of the

explanation.surface: A record-breaking amount concerning an incident from long ago.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A sight' is British for a lot, as in 'a sight better'. The record is the old 78 rpm gramophone disc.
explanation.definitionFit: Old gramophone discs played at 78 revolutions per minute, so a record of that type is named by the number.
